answer: In the PCA of the twelve forms of capital measured across the 39 hundred-year time slices (capital.csv, 4300–500 BCE), the three symbolic capital components — house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords — are characterized as follows. All three load positively on PC1 and therefore covary together with the dominant, economy-wide axis of capital accumulation, but they are not its strongest drivers: hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert) have a PC1 coefficient of +0.30 (rank 5/12 by |PC1|), daggers (ZDolch) +0.27 (rank 6/12), and house size (Zhausgr) +0.23 (rank 10/12), whereas copper/gold (+0.41), pottery decoration (+0.38) and pottery form (−0.35) dominate PC1 (30.3% of variance). Their distribution across PC2 is their distinguishing feature: daggers (PC2 +0.07) and hatchets/swords (PC2 +0.05) sit essentially on the PC1 axis, both close to the PC2 origin (ranked 10th and last, 12th, of the 12 components by |PC2 loading|), whereas house size loads much more strongly and positively on PC2 (+0.33, rank 5th; correlation 0.50). In the PC1–PC2 loading plane the hatchet/sword vector lies only ~10° from the PC1 axis and the dagger vector ~16°, just ~5° apart from each other, while house size is rotated ~40–46° away toward the PC2 axis (≈55.5° from PC1). So: daggers and hatchets/swords are characterized by positive PC1 with virtually no PC2 spread, while house size, also positive on PC1, is the symbolic-capital component that spreads most distinctly along PC2, tracking PC2's century-level swing (PC2 scores range −3.65 at 4300–4100 BCE to +2.50 at 3200 BCE, with the highest mean PC2 in the Middle Neolithic +1.80 and lowest in the Younger Bronze Age −1.12). PC sign is arbitrary; interpretations rest on relative signs and magnitudes. (PC1 λ=3.64, 30.3%; PC2 λ=2.34, 19.5%; PC1+PC2 = 49.8%.)

payload.hypothesis: In the PCA of twelve forms of capital across the 39 hundred-year time slices (4300–500 BCE), house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords all load positively on PC1 (hatchets/swords +0.30, daggers +0.27, house size +0.23), meaning they covary together with the dominant axis of capital accumulation, though none is the strongest PC1 driver (ranks 5/6/10 of 12). Their distinguishing feature is their distribution across PC2: daggers (+0.07) and hatchets/swords (+0.05) hug the PC1 axis with near-zero PC2 loadings (ranked 10th and 12th), whereas house size loads strongly and positively on PC2 (+0.33, rank 5th, correlation 0.50), so in the PC1–PC2 plane house size is rotated ~40–46° away from daggers and hatchets/swords. House size is therefore the symbolic capital component that spreads along PC2, while daggers and hatchets/swords are essentially PC1-only components.
payload.workflow: 1) Parsed capital.csv (comma-decimal CSV) into a 39×12 Z-matrix (39 century slices × 12 capital forms). 2) Standardized each variable and ran SVD-based PCA on the pooled slices (correlation-based); fixed the arbitrary PC sign by making the largest-|loading| variable positive per PC. 3) Extracted PC1/PC2 loadings, correlation loadings, explained variance, and per-century PC1/PC2 scores; computed loading-vector angles from the PC1 axis and the PC2 score distribution/group means. 4) Characterized ZAxtSchwert, ZDolch, Zhausgr via PC1 sign/magnitude/rank and PC2 placement/spread. 5) Consistency: confirmed capital.csv's 37 overlapping rows equal time_series raw values exactly (max abs diff 0.0 over 444 cells) and that a 37-row PCA on either source gives identical loadings; reported the 39-vs-37 sensitivity. 6) Pollen openness data excluded (environment context, not a capital form). Executed scripts: analysis_pca_capital.py (main analysis), supplementary.py (angular spread + artifact export).
